questions.stem: What is the main function of the spleen in the immune system?
choices: It filters blood and traps microorganisms
It is the site of T-lymphocyte maturation
questions.solution: The spleen acts as a filter for the blood, trapping blood-borne microorganisms. This function helps in the immune response by removing pathogens from the bloodstream. The other options are incorrect because antibodies are produced by B-cells, red blood cells are stored in the spleen but this is not its main function, and T-lymphocytes mature in the thymus, not the spleen.

hi.solution: स्प्लीन रक्त के लिए एक फिल्टर के रूप में कार्य करता है, रक्त-वाहक रोगाणुओं को फंसाता है। यह कार्य प्रतिरक्षा प्रतिक्रिया में रक्त प्रवाह से रोगजनकों को हटाकर सहायता करता है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि एंटीबॉडी B-कोशिकाओं द्वारा उत्पन्न किए जाते हैं, लाल रक्त कोशिकाओं को स्प्लीन में भंडारित किया जाता है लेकिन यह इसका मुख्य कार्य नहीं है, और T-लिम्फोसाइट्स थाइमस में परिपक्व होते हैं, न कि स्प्लीन में।

questions.stem: Which of the following is a method used for early cancer detection?
questions.solution: A biopsy is a method used for early cancer detection because it involves examining tissue samples to identify cancerous cells. Vaccination, exercise, and meditation are not methods used to detect cancer but rather ways to prevent or manage health conditions.

questions.stem: What is the main cause of death among non-infectious diseases?
questions.solution: Cancer is the main cause of death among non-infectious diseases because it involves the uncontrolled growth of abnormal cells that can spread throughout the body, leading to severe health complications. AIDS is caused by a virus and is classified as an infectious disease. Typhoid fever is also an infectious disease caused by bacteria. Alcohol abuse, while harmful, is not a disease itself but a behavior that can lead to various health issues.

questions.stem: Which type of immunity is developed when a person is given ready-made antibodies to fight an infection?
questions.solution: Passive immunity is developed when ready-made antibodies are given to a person. This provides immediate but short-term protection. Active immunity, on the other hand, is developed when the body produces its own antibodies. Innate and acquired immunity are broader categories that include both active and passive forms.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a pathogen?
questions.solution: A bacterium is a pathogen because it is an organism that can cause disease. Pathogens are living organisms that invade the body and lead to illness. A healthy person, a vaccine, and a symptom do not fit this definition, as they are not disease-causing agents.

questions.stem: What is the role of the female Anopheles mosquito in the life cycle of Plasmodium?
choices: It is the only host for the parasite
It is the vector that transmits the parasite to humans
It is the site where the parasite multiplies in the human body
It is the source of the toxic substance haemozoin
questions.solution: The female Anopheles mosquito acts as the vector, transmitting the malarial parasite to humans through its bite. It is not the only host, nor is it the site of multiplication in humans. Haemozoin is a toxic substance released when red blood cells rupture.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disease that is fatal and is caused by a virus?
questions.solution: AIDS is a fatal disease caused by a virus, specifically the HIV virus, which attacks the immune system. Typhoid fever is caused by bacteria, cancer is a group of diseases involving abnormal cell growth, and diabetes is a metabolic disorder, not caused by a virus.
